proposed_core_edits.reason: The representation-frontier question is nonessential to the proved identification spine and has generated two rejected overclaims. Deleting it without replacement leaves the proved complete-response cut-capacity lemma and the limited projected-incidence obstruction intact, while avoiding any unsupported characterization of the full joint system.

prose_updates.honest_scope: The compatibility-onset proposition, central sharpness theorem, finite nonrectangularity diagnostic, majority threshold, and complete-response reduction are proved. Every conditional response law and feasible-set row is restricted to \(\mathcal C_{+}\); null strata contribute zero target mass. Majority benefit is interpreted only for finite \(\Gamma\ge\Gamma_{\mathrm{feas}}\); smaller values represent infeasible response models. In the complete-response fixed-marginal special case, the finite-relation max-flow construction returns an attaining coupling and an explanatory minimum cut. Separately, the three-coordinate example is only a diagnostic for the incidence matrix obtained by projecting onto the arm-completion coordinates \(q_a\): its determinant-two minor is not asserted to occur in the full \(E,G_{\Gamma}\) system, does not exclude auxiliary-variable or extended formulations, and does not show that endpoint-attaining couplings are extreme points. No general network-matrix or balanced-hypergraph representation frontier is claimed. Empirical usefulness at \(106\) clusters and access to a fixed PPACT cohort remain outside this identification core.
